hook.text: Containers changed cloud computing. Now WebAssembly (Wasm) promises to change it again — faster, smaller, more portable.

buildup.text: Wasm is a binary format that runs anywhere — browsers, servers, or edge — at near-native speed, safely sandboxed.

discovery.text: Wasm modules start in microseconds (not milliseconds), use megabytes (not gigabytes), and have no OS dependency.

twist.text: Docker's co-founder said: 'If Wasm existed in 2008, we wouldn't have needed Docker.' That's how big the shift could be.

climax.text: Fermyon, Cosmonic, and Fastly run Wasm in production. It's not replacing containers — it fills gaps they can't.

punchline.text: Wasm starts in microseconds. Docker's creator wishes he had it first.

quiz.question: What advantage does WebAssembly have over containers?
options: Wasm modules start in microseconds and use far less memory than containers
Wasm completely replaces all container technology
Wasm only works in web browsers and has no server-side applications

details.summary: WebAssembly is emerging as a cloud compute primitive that starts faster than containers, uses less memory, and runs securely sandboxed code. WASI standardizes system access, enabling WebAssembly modules to run on servers, at the edge, and in browsers with near-native performance.
details.whyItMatters: WebAssembly could become the next evolution beyond containers for cloud workloads. Its security sandbox, portability, and startup speed make it ideal for edge computing and serverless functions.
takeaways: WebAssembly starts in microseconds, faster than containers
It runs sandboxed with capability-based security by default
WASI enables server-side and edge WebAssembly applications

faq.question: Will WebAssembly replace containers?
faq.answer: Not entirely. WebAssembly excels for short-lived, security-sensitive, and edge workloads where startup speed matters. Containers remain better for long-running services, complex applications, and workloads requiring full OS capabilities. Both will coexist as complementary technologies.

faq.question: Where is WebAssembly used in cloud today?
faq.answer: Cloudflare Workers use WebAssembly for edge functions. Fermyon Spin and Wasmtime power server-side WebAssembly. Envoy proxy uses WASM for extensible filters. Plugin systems in databases and edge platforms use WASM for safe third-party code execution.
